Title: The Drowned Bell
Rumor: The Drowned Bell. Boatmen claim that a great bronze bell lies beneath the Storbruhn near an abandoned river crossing. On certain nights, its tolling can be heard through the water, though no vessel has ever recovered it. Some believe it belonged to a temple destroyed by a catastrophic flood, while others insist the bell is rung by the dead.
First lead: Old river pilots know a deep channel where the sound is most frequently reported.

Title: The Island That Walks
Rumor: The Island That Walks. Fishermen on Lake Ophar tell of a wooded island that appears in different places from one season to the next. Its trees are unusually old, and its shores are said to conceal the ruins of a small stone settlement. A few Namaris stories describe the island as a living creature that sleeps for centuries at a time.
First lead: Lake fishermen sometimes mark its supposed sightings on their navigation charts.

Title: The Ferryman's Last Passage
Rumor: The Ferryman's Last Passage. According to river tradition, a ghostly ferry crosses a remote stretch of the Storbruhn on moonless nights. Its passengers are silent, and its ferryman accepts only coins bearing the likeness of a long-dead ruler. Those who board are supposedly carried to a landing that disappeared generations ago.
First lead: An abandoned ferry landing downstream of Westbridge is associated with the tale.

Title: The Sunken Palace
Rumor: The Sunken Palace. Namaris legends describe the ruins of a magnificent palace lying beneath the waters of Lake Ophar, built before their ancestors first settled the lake. Its halls contain statues of unfamiliar rulers and mosaics depicting an ancient kingdom. Some claim that a portion of the palace rises above the water during exceptionally low lake levels.
First lead: Namaris historians know traditional descriptions of the palace's location.

Title: The Crown of Mudcrown
Rumor: The Crown of Mudcrown. Travelers among the marshes whisper that the current Mudcrown king possesses an ancient crown recovered from a ruined temple beneath the bog. The crown is supposedly far older than the frogfolk kingdom and grants its wearer authority over certain creatures of the marsh. Others suspect that the royal treasure is merely a particularly elaborate collection of bones and river shells.
First lead: Frogfolk storytellers disagree enthusiastically about which king first acquired the crown.

Title: The Ship of Seven Lanterns
Rumor: The Ship of Seven Lanterns. A narrow river vessel bearing seven blue lanterns occasionally appears on the Storbruhn, traveling silently against the current. Those who approach report finding no crew aboard. An old Ballantyre river-marine account describes a similar vessel encountered during the War of Broken Banners, though the ship supposedly sank years before.
First lead: Retired river marines and older pilots remember sightings near a broad bend below Westbridge.

Title: The Pearl of Ophar
Rumor: The Pearl of Ophar. Namaris divers speak of an enormous pearl resting within a submerged cavern beneath Lake Ophar. Its light is said to illuminate the waters around it, attracting strange creatures from the deepest parts of the lake. One legend claims that the pearl was placed there to mark the resting place of a beloved ancient ruler.
First lead: Vellis Duskfin knows several peaceful Namaris accounts of the cavern, though their details differ.

Title: The Reed King's Tomb
Rumor: The Reed King's Tomb. Ssaresh tradition describes a forgotten ruler buried beneath a great mound surrounded by reeds. The tomb was supposedly sealed with stone doors and protected by carvings of serpents and crocodiles. During the annual floods, unusual ornaments and fragments of worked stone sometimes wash from the mound's slopes.
First lead: Ssaresh elders preserve different accounts of the tomb's location in the lower marshlands.

Title: The Vanished Customs House
Rumor: The Vanished Customs House. An old stone customs post once stood along a remote river channel, collecting tolls from passing merchants. It was abandoned after the channel shifted and eventually disappeared from modern maps. Boatmen claim its strongroom was never emptied and that its ledgers still contain records of cargo whose owners vanished during the war.
First lead: An old commercial chart in Westbridge depicts the former channel and landing.

Title: The River Dragon
Rumor: The River Dragon. Fishermen describe an enormous serpentine creature inhabiting the deepest reaches of the Storbruhn. It rarely attacks boats but occasionally surfaces beneath the moon, its scales gleaming like wet copper. Several captains claim to have seen it swallow entire nets, while a Namaris tradition holds that the creature guards an ancient underwater passage.
First lead: Tobin Sedge has heard several apparently independent accounts of sightings near the same river gorge.

Title: The Stone Road Beneath the Lake
Rumor: The Stone Road Beneath the Lake. During particularly clear weather, sailors claim to see a paved road far below the surface of Lake Ophar. It extends toward the ruins of buildings whose outlines can only be glimpsed from above. Some Namaris historians believe the road predates the present shoreline, suggesting that the lake once covered a much smaller area.
First lead: A Namaris navigation chart marks a region of unusually clear, shallow water.

Title: The Lost Ballantyre Payroll
Rumor: The Lost Ballantyre Payroll. A vessel carrying military pay for northern soldiers supposedly vanished on the Storbruhn during the final years of the War of Broken Banners. Stories differ as to whether it sank, was captured by river pirates, or was deliberately hidden by its own crew. The pay chest is said to contain enough silver to purchase a considerable estate.
First lead: Old Ballantyre marines remember the ship's name and the stretch of river where it disappeared.

Title: The Lantern Marsh
Rumor: The Lantern Marsh. Pale green lights sometimes drift across the wetlands south of Westbridge, gathering above isolated pools and ruined stone structures. Local fishermen claim the lights mark places where travelers drowned, while Ssaresh stories associate them with ancient spirits of the marsh. Those who follow them occasionally return carrying unfamiliar coins or ornaments.
First lead: A Ssaresh fishing route passes near the marsh where the lights are most often seen.

Title: The Singing Shell
Rumor: The Singing Shell. Among the Namaris there is a legend of a great conch shell whose sound can be heard throughout Lake Ophar when sounded beneath the water. It was supposedly hidden in a submerged shrine generations ago. Certain stories suggest that the shell summons the lake's guardians, while others claim it merely reveals the location of ancient underwater roads.
First lead: Namaris merchants occasionally sell small carvings depicting the legendary shell.

Title: The Forgotten Lockworks
Rumor: The Forgotten Lockworks. River pilots speak of an abandoned system of stone locks and channels constructed by an unknown civilization. Its surviving gates are enormous, and some are said to move without assistance during unusual changes in water level. No one agrees upon why the works were abandoned or what settlement they once served.
First lead: An older river chart marks several unexplained masonry structures beside a disused channel.

Title: The Eel Queen's Garden
Rumor: The Eel Queen's Garden. Frogfolk legends describe a hidden garden deep within the marsh where enormous lilies grow upon black water. The garden is supposedly tended by an ancient creature known as the Eel Queen, whose favor brings abundant fishing and whose displeasure brings floods. Mudcrown courtiers insist that their royal family has visited the garden for generations.
First lead: Lady Vromma Miretongue is rumored to know a ceremonial route leading toward the garden.

Title: The Emberhearth Ancestors
Rumor: The Emberhearth Ancestors. Dwarven craftsmen sometimes speak of an ancient workshop far upriver where their ancestors produced metalwork of unmatched quality. The site was abandoned centuries ago, but its surviving furnaces and tools supposedly remain concealed within a ruined riverside structure. Recently, manufactured goods bearing similar patterns have begun appearing in the markets of Westbridge.
First lead: Mira Stoneward possesses sketches comparing the old designs with modern imported metalwork.

Title: The River's Forgotten Mouth
Rumor: The River's Forgotten Mouth. An ancient map shows the Storbruhn entering Lake Ophar through a channel now occupied by dense marsh and shallow pools. Ssaresh tradition maintains that the old waterway still exists beneath the reeds and can be navigated during exceptional floods. Some believe the channel leads to a buried settlement once connected to the lake by boat.
First lead: Ishkara Silt-Eye knows older stories describing the route of the lost channel.

Title: The Moonlit Market
Rumor: The Moonlit Market. Boatmen occasionally speak of a strange market that appears upon a remote river island on nights when the moon is full. Merchants there sell unfamiliar goods, accept unusual forms of payment, and depart before dawn. Those who have visited disagree about whether the traders are elves, spirits, or ordinary smugglers maintaining an elaborate deception.
First lead: The same isolated island appears in several old pilots' accounts, though under different names.

Title: The Last Light of Ophar
Rumor: The Last Light of Ophar. At the southern edge of Lake Ophar, a solitary light sometimes appears far beyond the usual shipping lanes. It resembles the lantern of a distant lighthouse, although no lighthouse is known to stand there. Some Namaris legends describe an ancient tower built upon a submerged island, while human sailors insist that the light marks a route through dangerous waters to a forgotten harbor.
First lead: A handful of experienced lake captains have recorded the light's bearing in their logs.
